_comment: Template for the operator dead-man switch. Copy to
~/.config/fleet/deadman.json and chmod 600 — the real file names your
contacts and holds an SMTP password, and this repo is public.
Stages fire in ascending after_hours order, once each, and reset when you
run `deadman.py alive`. Write every body yourself: these are the words
someone reads when you cannot be reached, and no agent should be

smtp._comment: Gmail: use an app password, not your account password.

_life_signals: Checked by `check --corroborate` before anything is sent. If one of
these is fresher than the silence, the clock moves back to that moment
and the ladder is re-evaluated from there.
ONLY LIST THINGS A HUMAN CAUSES. This fleet writes events.jsonl around
the clock from fleet/codex/hermes, so treating the event log as proof of
life would build a switch that can never fire — worse than none, because
you would trust it. Machine activity proves the machine is up. Nothing
The git signal is the weak one: an agent committing as you is
indistinguishable from you. Only list repos nothing automated commits to
Empty by default. An unconfigured switch escalates on the clock alone,
which is the safe direction to be wrong in.

life_signals.label: nostr
_note: Your PERSONAL npub, not the fleet's key in ~/.config/fleet/nostr.nsec.
The fleet posts on a schedule; that would prove the cron job is alive.
Needs the venv interpreter — relay reads use websocket-client, which
the system python does not have. See the cron line in the README.

life_signals.label: shell history
life_signals._note: written when an interactive shell exits, not live during one

_thresholds: Calibrated to an operator who does not go more than a week without
giving notice. A week of quiet is therefore normal and must stay silent;
the ladder starts only once silence has become genuinely unusual.
Resist tightening these. A switch that fires during an ordinary quiet
stretch teaches everyone on the list to ignore it, and it is the same
list you need to believe the one real message.

_comment: 5 days: you only, on your own phone. Nobody else hears this. It is a
reminder that the switch exists and is counting, while there is still
plenty of room to reset it.
stages.subject: check-in overdue
stages.body: No check-in for 5 days. Run: deadman.py alive

_comment: 8 days: past your own stated normal, so the first human hears it.
Your deputy, not your family — this is still far more likely to be a
lost phone than an emergency, and it should reach someone who can
stages.subject: No check-in from <name> for 8 days
stages.body: REPLACE THIS. Say who you are, that this is an automated message from <name>'s own machine, that <name> does not normally go more than a week without notice, when they were last heard from, and exactly what you want checked first.

_comment: 12 days: family. Written for someone who does not know what this
system is and is about to be frightened by it — say so in the first
line. Four days after the deputy, so there was time to stand it down.
stages.subject: REPLACE THIS
stages.body: REPLACE THIS ENTIRELY. Suggested shape: this is an automated message set up in advance by <name>, sent by their own computer; it sends only after 12 days with no check-in; it does not mean something has happened; here is who has already been contacted, who to call, and what is known about the travel plan.
